properties.foundation_analysis: Subterranean Carboniferous sedimentary bedrock overlain by glacial till. Primary building fabric comprises fine-grained, pale blonde to buff Craigleith and Hailes quartzose sandstone. Masonry bound with traditional non-hydraulic to weakly hydraulic lime and sharp quartz sand mortar.

properties.primary_surfacing: Engineered roadway and paved pedestrian curbs
properties.wear_characteristics: Authentic environmental patina and drainage grading

properties.botanical_analysis: Central crescent garden interior populated by mature *Platanus × acerifolia* (London plane) and *Acer pseudoplatanus* (Sycamore). September 24 late-summer to early-autumn phenology: dense canopies exhibiting initial leaf chlorosis, yellowing outer margins, and early dispersed litterfall over dense *Lolium perenne* and *Festuca rubra* lawn.

properties.architectural_summary: Curved Georgian Neo-Classical residential circus terrace (c. 1822, James Gillespie Graham). Massing forms a four-storey continuous concave elevation over sunken basement lightwells. Ground floor exhibits channelled V-jointed ashlar rustication; upper storeys feature polished ashlar with continuous string courses, moulded architraves, Doric/Ionic pilaster rhythm, full entablature, and parapet blocking course. Regular fenestration grid of multi-pane 6-over-6 and 12-over-12 painted timber sash-and-case windows. Pitched roofs clad in Scottish slate with regular sandstone ashlar chimney stacks.
